headline: Paid reweighting improves all three n35 primal endpoints beyond both controls, with mixed proof costs; keep it default off and recommend only future independent limited confirmation.
rationale: The fixed C recipe improves true final U over both B and matched M on C35 (0.120201245 versus 0.148022963), B35 (0.187861163 versus 0.219720788) and X35 (0.466514935 versus B 0.518363903 and M 0.511546413). B35 also raises qualified L slightly. C35 and X35 instead lose lower-bound strength, and all n35 arms remain OPEN. All three methods certify the n20 roles, while C20-C takes about219.5s versus211.5/211.1s for B/M. Thus there is an end-to-end original-objective primal signal beyond restarting, not complete dominance or robust acceleration. Keep the fixed candidate as a research option for a future independently preregistered, finite confirmation with matched restart and protection roles; this task starts no such run.
paper_interpretation: C improves final U beyond both controls on all three n35 roles, with a small B35 lower-bound gain and weaker C35/X35 lowers. All n35 runs remain open. All methods certify the n20 roles; C20-C takes about219.5s versus211.5/211.1s for B/M. Matched M also improves the paid X35 primal endpoint despite its unchanged H Start. These endpoint gains warrant only future independent limited confirmation of the fixed default-off recipe, not default promotion or a claim of uniform acceleration.
